chunks: And from him, from Musa ibn al-Hasan, from Ahmad ibn Hilal, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Ali ibn 'Atiyyah, who said:

We departed from Al-Muzdalifah at night, I and Hisham ibn Abd al-Malik al-Kufi, and Hisham was anxious. We arrived at Jamarat al-Aqabah at the rising of Fajr. Hisham said to me, 'What have we innovated in our Hajj? We are still in this state.' Then we met Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), who had already thrown the pebbles at the Jamarat and had departed. Hisham's heart was comforted.
If he forgot to throw the pebbles at the Jamarat until he reached Mecca, he should return and throw them.

key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ مُوسَى: Abu al-Hasan Musa, referring to Imam Musa al-Kazim (peace be upon him).
key_terms.الْمُزْدَلِفَة: Al-Muzdalifah, a plain near Mecca where pilgrims spend the night after leaving Mina.
key_terms.جَمْرَة الْعَقَبَة: Jamarat al-Aqabah, the largest of the three pillars where pilgrims throw pebbles during Hajj.
key_terms.رَمْي الْجِمَار: Ramy al-Jimar, the ritual of stoning the devil by throwing pebbles at the Jamarat pillars.
key_terms.طَابَتْ نَفْس: His heart was comforted/soothed (idiom for relief from anxiety).

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim forgets to throw pebbles at Jamarat al-Aqabah until they have already reached Mecca?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the practical jurisprudence of Hajj timing, specifically addressing the anxiety of delaying the stoning of Jamarat al-Aqabah until after Fajr. It establishes the legal principle that if a pilgrim forgets to stone the pillars before departing for Mea, they are obligated to return to Mina to complete the ritual, ensuring the validity of their Hajj. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on adhering to the Prophet's Sunnah and the Imams' guidance in resolving minor ritual uncertainties.
